entityDescription: TimeTech, GmbH, (private limited liability company) was founded in 1990 as a spinoff of the University of Stuttgart’s Institute for Navigation under Professor Hartl. From 1990 to 2000, the company was located in the Stuttgart Technology Center, and is now situated in the Stuttgart Engineering Park. TimeTech was established amidst a vibrant European engagement in Space programs and with the anticipation of growing German interest in the field of Earth navigation. While still at the University, the team developed and carried out successful experiments in the following areas: - Intercontinental time transfer between national measurement laboratories, such as the Physikalisch-Technische Bundesanstalt (PTB), Braunschweig (PTB), and - Highly precise in-orbit satellite location. The two technologies pioneered by the team are even today acknowledged to be leading, worldwide. The primary customers for the satellite orbit determination measurement instruments produced by TimeTech are satellite operators, like the Societé Européenne des Satéllites, (SES in Luxembourg, operators of the ASTRA Satellites), Telenor and the Indian Space Research Organisation. SES have used TimeTech’s instruments in operation for more than 15 years for the highly precise positioning of the ASTRA Satellites. TimeTech has also engineered and supplied the instruments for precision time and frequency transfer for comparison of atomic clocks using intercontinental links by national time laboratories in the USA, Europe and Asia. TimeTech is currently engaged in technology projects such as ACES: Atomic Clock Ensemble in Space, both in the flight and ground segments, and has supplied atomic clock based Frequency and Time Systems (F&T) to the Deep Space Network Stations of the European Space Agency (ESA). TimeTech’s supplied instruments are on-board the International Space Station (ISS), ERS-2, Rosetta and the Venus Express satellites.

entityDescription: About Arctic Business Incubator Arctic Business Incubator (ABI) is Sweden’s northernmost business incubator with operations from Skellefteå in the south to Kiruna in the north – an area covering 20 municipalities, 300,000 inhabitants and 20 per cent of Sweden’s total area. Our task is to develop entrepreneurs and their innovative business ideas into profitable and vibrant international growth companies. ABI works with ideas from all industries that meet our criteria. The ideas come for example from individual entrepreneurs, Luleå University of Technology, institutions and research organisations as well as existing companies. ABI was set up in Luleå in 2005 in Luleå and is a Swedish limited liability company owned equally by LTU Holding, Norrlandsfonden, Norrbotten County Council (NLL) and the municipalities of Luleå and Skellefteå. Our operations are financed by the owners, by Vinnova Excellence program – an initiative targeting a small selection of the best business incubators in Sweden. ABI is a member of SISP, a trade organisation for Sweden’s business incubators and science parks, with 65 members all over Sweden which together host more than 5,000 companies with about 72,000 employees. ABI is also host for the Swedish national space incubator, ESA-BIC Sweden, upon assignment by ESA and Swedish National Space Board.

entityDescription: The Royal Belgian Institute for Space Aeronomy (BIRA-IASB) is a Belgian federal scientific research institute. Our scientists rely on ground-based, balloon-, air- or space-borne instruments and computer models. entityDescription:
Biomed d.o.o. was established in 1989. It maintains a baromedical laboratory for the treatment of decompression sickness and testing of hyperbaric equipment. It has also developed a facility for the evaluation of breathing apparatus according to International Standards (ISO). It also has a testing laboratory for the testing of thermal and evaporative resistance of clothing, particularly personal protective equipment. BIOMED designs and develops a variety of manikins for specific testing of equipment in extreme environments. Recently, it has assisted in the design and development of hypoxic facilities manufactured by Van Amerongen (VA), and marketed by b-Cat (both from The Netherlands). 
Biomed coordinated military and industrial projects focussing on the protection of Armed Forces Personnel from extreme environments. In collaboration with the CNRS Laboratory in Strasbourg, it has conducted extensive tests of thermal and evaporative resistance of garment assemblies designed for both desert, and Alpine conditions using a thermal manikin. With Prof. Wissler from the University of Texas it has assisted in the further development of a thermoregulatory model, which is now being considered for use in a collaborative project with the Institute of Biometeorology in Florence to test the concept of the Universal Thermal Climate Index, which is the aim of the COST 730 initiative.
Biomed d.o.o. maintains a research laboratory at the Planica Olympic Sports Centre. It has assisted in organising microgravity simulation studies and manages hypoxic training studies at the Olympic Sport Centre Planica. It has also assisted in the testing of fire retardant protective clothing for the UK Ministry of Defence, and has acted as consultant to W.L. Gore & Associates, evaluating prototype clothing ensembles. Biomed personnel have assisted in the ESA PECS project Lunar Habitat Simulation, and the FP7 project Planetary Habitat Simulaiton

Terradue UK Ltd will soon have its offices in the Harwell Campus within the Innovations Technology Access Centre initiative supported by the STFC (Science & Technology Facilities Council. 
Terradue UK Ltd is currently establishing partnership and consortiums to bid on UK co-funded projects and sees ESA projects as an opportunity to staff the subsidiary in the Harwell campus where ESA has just open a centre. entityDescription:
VRVis is Austria's leading research center in the field of visual computing. Our team, comprising more than 80 employees, works with great commitment on innovative application-oriented research and development projects. As a COMET Competence Center, we pursue the goal of building a bridge between research and practice with our partners from science, business and industry.
VRVis GmbH is funded by BMIMI, BMWET, Tyrol, Vorarlberg and Vienna Business Agency in the scope of COMET - Competence Centers for Excellent Technologies (911654) which is managed by FFG.
Our research focus at VRVis is visual computing: we present data, connections, and questions in the best possible visual and interactive form to make decisions easier. Images are a universal means of communication. Who sees, understands.As a COMET Competence Center, our mission at VRVis is to build a bridge from science to industry. In basic research, our seven specialized groups work on visionary solutions and new findings in the field of high technology. Our researchers regularly publish in high impact publications and give lectures at international conferences. VRVis employees have received several awards for their groundbreaking research work. Also, over 30 patents have already been applied for at VRVis.
In applied industrial projects, we advance the state-of-tech and thus help our industry partners to achieve a decisive technological lead. Our research topics range from data science and computer vision to artificial intelligence and virtual reality.
In addition to our own basic research, we work closely with the TU Wien, the TU Graz, and the University of Vienna. Together we form one of the largest research clusters in Europe specializing in visual computing. Besides our close collaboration with these three universities, we also cooperate with a number of international research institutions, such as University of Stuttgart, ETH Zürich, University of Magdeburg, University of Utah, and many more.

entityName: Bavarian Center for Applied Energy Research e.V. (ZAE Bayern)
entityDescription:
The Bavarian Center for Applied Energy Research e.V. (ZAE Bayern) is a non-university research institute with approx. 180 employees, which receives institutional funding from the Bavarian Ministry of Economic Affairs, Regional Development and Energy. We offer our customers complete innovation packages in the field of efficient and sustainable energy systems. In its core competence areas of renewable energies, energy storage and energy efficiency, ZAE Bayern combines materials research, component development and system optimization into a seamless value-added chain in an interdisciplinary research approach. The researchers at ZAE Bayern work at the interface between basic research and applied industrial research and deal, among other things, with nanomaterials, thermal and electrochemical energy storage, energy-efficient processes, photovoltaics, energy-optimised buildings and urban areas as well as smart grids and cross-sectoral energy systems (electricity and heat/cooling). 
For over 25 years, ZAE Bayern has been a registered association based in Würzburg. In December 1991, the founding members set themselves the goal of promoting energy research and providing training, education, consulting service, information, and documentation in all areas relevant to energy technology and its related sciences. To date, ZAE Bayern has developed into a nationally and internationally recognized research institute. Our employees, who are scientists, technical staff, administrative employees and students, make a decisive contribution to this.

entityDescription: The Foundation for Climate and Sustainability (FCS), recognized by the Tuscany Region as an institute of research and accreditation, was created in 1994 to develop studies and activities in the field of meteorology, climatology, monitoring and conservation of natural resources, sustainability of land management and planning processes. Over the years, the Foundation has also specialized in the valorisation of artistic craftsmanship, providing support to artisan companies in the search for innovative and sustainable technological solutions, and in experimenting with new methods in the textile sector, based on a production model Of quality related to the territory. FCS has always been involved in research and technology transfer projects with the main local and national authorities, including the Tuscany Region, the Florence Province, the University of Florence, the Florence Cassa di Risparmio, the Osservatorio degli Artisti d'Arte, the italian National Research Center (CNR), the Academy of Georgofili, the Union of Municipalities, Agricultural Consortia, Professional Organizations and International bodies such as the European Commision and the European Space Agency.

entityDescription:
ACRI-HE is a company of the ACRI-Group, with ACRI-ST as majority shareholder, which was founded by bringing together the environmental studies of ACRI-ST with EO and the activity of HOCER in environmental in-situ surveys and modeling (e.g. sedimentology, bathymetry, oceanography). The rationale of this merger is to have a dedicated structure fully focused on the development and exploitation of emerging EO-derived services in the COPERNICUS context. ACRI-HE has a subsidiary in Morocco, since 2006, to develop the African services.
ACRI-HE performs research activities related to theoretical and numerical fluid dynamics, geophysics, ocean and atmosphere modelling, develops and operates information services related to the surveillance and forecast of the Earth environment, especially for the water quality monitoring (ocean, coastal and inland water). ACRI-HE contributes to a wide scope of studies by local, national and international environmental agencies such as, analysis of user requirements, technological constraints study, analysis and implementation of solutions, estimation and monitoring of environmental, economic and social impacts.
